title: Who founded the Imperial Chola dynasty in the medieval period?
description: Identify the ruler who established the Imperial Chola dynasty in the 9th century CE.
hint: He captured Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars.
summary: Vijayalaya Chola is regarded as the founder of the Imperial Chola dynasty.

title: Which city became an important Chola capital under Vijayalaya Chola?
description: Identify the city captured by Vijayalaya Chola that became a major Chola center.
hint: It is located in present-day Tamil Nadu.
summary: Vijayalaya Chola captured Thanjavur and established it as an important Chola center.

title: Who was the father of Rajaraja Chola I?
description: Identify the Chola ruler who was the father of Rajaraja Chola I.
hint: He ruled before Rajaraja I.
summary: Sundara Chola, also known as Parantaka II, was the father of Rajaraja Chola I.

title: Who was one of the greatest rulers of the Chola Empire?
description: Identify the ruler whose reign marked major territorial, administrative and architectural achievements.
hint: He built the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur.
summary: Rajaraja Chola I was one of the greatest rulers of the Chola Empire.

title: When did Rajaraja Chola I begin his reign?
description: Identify the approximate year in which Rajaraja Chola I became ruler.
hint: His reign began near the end of the 10th century.
summary: Rajaraja Chola I began his reign in 985 CE.

title: Which temple was built by Rajaraja Chola I at Thanjavur?
description: Identify the famous temple constructed during the reign of Rajaraja Chola I.
hint: It is dedicated to Shiva.
summary: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur was built under Rajaraja Chola I.

title: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur is dedicated primarily to which deity?
description: Identify the principal deity worshipped in the Brihadisvara Temple.
hint: The temple is a major Shaiva monument.
summary: The Brihadisvara Temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

title: Which title was used by Rajaraja Chola I?
description: Identify a famous royal title associated with Rajaraja Chola I.
hint: It means something like king of kings.
summary: Rajaraja Chola I used the title Rajarajakesari.

title: Who succeeded Rajaraja Chola I?
description: Identify the ruler who succeeded Rajaraja Chola I.
hint: He was also a major conqueror.
summary: Rajendra Chola I succeeded Rajaraja Chola I.

title: Which Chola ruler led an expedition to the Ganges?
description: Identify the Chola ruler associated with the famous northern expedition reaching the Ganges.
hint: He founded Gangaikondacholapuram.
summary: Rajendra Chola I led an expedition toward the Ganges and adopted the title Gangaikonda Chola.

title: Which city was founded by Rajendra Chola I as his capital?
description: Identify the city established by Rajendra Chola I after his northern campaigns.
hint: Its name means the Chola who conquered the Ganga.
summary: Rajendra Chola I founded Gangaikondacholapuram as his capital.

title: Which Chola ruler conducted naval expeditions against Srivijaya?
description: Identify the ruler who launched a major naval expedition against the Srivijaya kingdom in Southeast Asia.
hint: The expedition took place in the early 11th century.
summary: Rajendra Chola I conducted a famous naval expedition against Srivijaya.

title: Srivijaya was primarily located in which region?
description: Identify the Southeast Asian region associated with the Srivijaya kingdom.
hint: It was centered around the Malay Archipelago.
summary: Srivijaya was a major maritime kingdom centered in Southeast Asia, especially Sumatra.

title: Which Chola ruler is associated with the conquest of northern Sri Lanka?
description: Identify the ruler whose reign saw major Chola expansion into Sri Lanka.
hint: He preceded Rajendra Chola I.
summary: Rajaraja Chola I conquered northern parts of Sri Lanka and incorporated them into the Chola realm.

title: Which island kingdom was heavily attacked by the Cholas?
description: Identify the island kingdom that became a major target of Chola expansion.
hint: It lies south of India.
summary: Sri Lanka was repeatedly attacked and partly conquered by the Cholas.

title: What was the ancient name of the Chola port city now known as Poompuhar?
description: Identify the historical name of the important Chola port at the mouth of the Kaveri.
hint: It appears in Sangam literature.
summary: Poompuhar was known as Kaveripattinam or Puhar.

title: Which river was especially important to the Chola heartland?
description: Identify the major river associated with the fertile Chola delta.
hint: Its delta is one of the most fertile regions of Tamil Nadu.
summary: The Kaveri River was central to Chola agriculture and prosperity.

title: Which Chola ruler is associated with the construction of Kallanai?
description: Identify the early Chola ruler traditionally credited with constructing the Grand Anicut across the Kaveri.
hint: He was an early Chola ruler from the Sangam period.
summary: Kallanai is traditionally attributed to Karikala Chola.

title: What was the main purpose of Kallanai?
description: Identify the primary function of the ancient Grand Anicut.
hint: It was constructed across the Kaveri River.
summary: Kallanai was constructed primarily to divert and regulate water for irrigation.

title: Which Chola ruler is associated with the famous bronze Nataraja tradition?
description: Identify the period in which Chola bronze sculpture reached exceptional artistic development.
hint: The tradition flourished particularly during the Imperial Chola period.
summary: Chola bronze sculpture, especially Nataraja images, flourished during the Imperial Chola period.

title: Which architectural style is strongly associated with Chola temples?
description: Identify the broad South Indian temple architectural tradition represented by major Chola temples.
hint: It developed prominently in the Tamil region.
summary: Chola temples are major examples of the Dravidian architectural tradition.

title: Which Chola temple is located at Gangaikondacholapuram?
description: Identify the major temple built by Rajendra Chola I at his new capital.
hint: It is also known as the temple of Gangaikondacholisvaram.
summary: The Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikondacholapuram was built by Rajendra Chola I.

title: Which Chola temple is located at Darasuram?
description: Identify the famous Chola temple situated at Darasuram near Kumbakonam.
hint: It is associated with Rajaraja II.
summary: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was built during the reign of Rajaraja II.

title: Which group of monuments includes three major Chola temples?
description: Identify the UNESCO World Heritage property that includes major Chola temples.
hint: The property includes temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram.
summary: The Great Living Chola Temples include three major Chola temples.

title: Which Chola ruler established a powerful local administrative system?
description: Identify the ruler whose reign provides extensive evidence of Chola administration through inscriptions.
hint: His inscriptions are found extensively at Thanjavur.
summary: Rajaraja Chola I strengthened and organized the Chola administrative system.

title: What was the village assembly of a Brahmadeya village called?
description: Identify the term used for the assembly of Brahmadeya villages in Chola administration.
hint: It was different from the general village assembly called ur.
summary: The assembly of a Brahmadeya village was known as sabha or mahasabha.

title: What was the general village assembly in Chola administration called?
description: Identify the village assembly that represented ordinary villages.
hint: It was distinct from sabha and nagaram.
summary: The general village assembly was called ur.

title: What was the assembly of merchants and townspeople called?
description: Identify the institution associated with urban centers and merchant groups.
hint: The term is associated with towns.
summary: Nagaram was an assembly associated with merchants and urban communities.

title: Which inscription is famous for describing Chola village self-government?
description: Identify the inscription that provides detailed information about village administration.
hint: It is found in present-day Tamil Nadu.
summary: The Uttaramerur inscriptions provide important evidence about Chola village administration.

title: Which method is associated with selection of members to Chola village committees?
description: Identify the method described in the Uttaramerur inscriptions.
hint: It involved drawing lots from eligible candidates.
summary: The Kudavolai system used a form of lot-drawing to select committee members.

title: What was a Brahmadeya in Chola administration?
description: Identify the type of settlement associated with land grants to Brahmins.
hint: The name literally refers to a grant associated with Brahmins.
summary: Brahmadeya referred to land or villages granted to Brahmins.

title: Which term referred to a major territorial unit in the Chola administration?
description: Identify the larger territorial division used in the Chola administrative system.
hint: It was larger than a nadu.
summary: Mandalam was a major territorial division in the Chola administrative structure.

title: Which group played an important role in Chola overseas trade?
description: Identify the merchant guilds associated with long-distance commerce during the Chola period.
hint: Examples include Ayyavole and Manigramam.
summary: Merchant guilds such as Ayyavole and Manigramam played important roles in trade.

title: Which merchant guild was known as the 'Five Hundred of Ayyavole'?
description: Identify the famous South Indian merchant organization.
hint: It was a prominent long-distance trading guild.
summary: Ayyavole was a famous merchant guild involved in long-distance trade.

title: Which crop was especially important to the Chola economy?
description: Identify the crop strongly associated with the fertile Kaveri delta.
hint: It is a staple food crop of South India.
summary: Rice cultivation was central to the agricultural economy of the Chola heartland.

title: Which deity was particularly prominent in Chola royal religious patronage?
description: Identify the deity whose worship was strongly represented in major Chola temples.
hint: The Brihadisvara temples are dedicated to this deity.
summary: Shiva received major royal patronage under the Cholas.

title: Which Buddhist monastery in Nagapattinam received Chola patronage?
description: Identify the famous Buddhist monastery associated with Chola-era patronage and Srivijayan connections.
hint: Its name is associated with a major Southeast Asian maritime kingdom.
summary: The Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam received patronage during the Chola period.

title: Which language dominated Chola inscriptions in the Tamil region?
description: Identify the major regional language used extensively in Chola inscriptions.
hint: It is the classical language of Tamil Nadu.
summary: Tamil was extensively used in Chola inscriptions in the Tamil region.

title: Which literary work is associated with Kamban?
description: Identify the famous Tamil epic composed by the medieval poet Kamban.
hint: It is a Tamil rendering of the Ramayana tradition.
summary: Kamban composed the Ramavataram, commonly known as Kamba Ramayanam.

title: Which Shaiva devotional text was compiled during the Chola period?
description: Identify the collection of Tamil Shaiva hymns associated with the Nayanars.
hint: It is known as the Tamil Shaiva canon.
summary: The Tirumurai is the canonical collection of Tamil Shaiva devotional hymns.

title: Who compiled the Shaiva devotional hymns into the Tirumurai?
description: Identify the Chola-era scholar traditionally credited with collecting and organizing the Shaiva hymns.
hint: He served under Rajaraja Chola I.
summary: Nambiyandar Nambi is traditionally credited with compiling the Shaiva hymns into the Tirumurai.

title: Who wrote the Periyapuranam?
description: Identify the Tamil literary work and its author associated with the Chola period.
hint: He served under Kulottunga II.
summary: Sekkizhar wrote the Periyapuranam, a major Shaiva hagiographical work.

title: Which dynasty was a major rival of the Cholas in the Deccan?
description: Identify the dynasty that frequently conflicted with the Cholas over control of the Deccan.
hint: Its capital was Kalyani.
summary: The Western Chalukyas of Kalyani were major rivals of the Cholas.

title: Which Chola ruler fought the Western Chalukyas at the Battle of Koppam?
description: Identify the Chola ruler who died during the Battle of Koppam.
hint: He was the elder brother of Rajendra II.
summary: Rajadhiraja Chola I died during the Battle of Koppam against the Western Chalukyas.

title: Which Chola ruler defeated the Western Chalukyas at the Battle of Takkolam?
description: Identify the Chola ruler associated with the Chola defeat at Takkolam.
hint: He was the son of Parantaka I.
summary: Rajaditya Chola, son of Parantaka I, was killed at the Battle of Takkolam in 949 CE.

title: Which ruler is associated with the Chola conquest of the Maldives?
description: Identify the Chola ruler whose expansion included the conquest of the Maldives.
hint: He was one of the most powerful Chola emperors.
summary: Rajaraja Chola I is associated with the Chola conquest of the Maldives.

title: Which Chola ruler is known for his naval expedition to Southeast Asia?
description: Identify the ruler whose naval power extended Chola influence into Southeast Asian maritime routes.
hint: His expedition targeted Srivijaya.
summary: Rajendra Chola I is especially known for his naval expedition against Srivijaya.

title: Which dynasty succeeded the Later Cholas in the Tamil region?
description: Identify the dynasty that rose to prominence after the decline of Chola power.
hint: Its capital was Madurai.
summary: The Pandyas eventually emerged as the dominant power in the Tamil region after the decline of the Cholas.

title: Which factor contributed significantly to the strength of the Chola state?
description: Identify an important economic foundation of Chola power.
hint: Think about the fertile Kaveri delta.
summary: Agricultural productivity, especially in the Kaveri delta, provided an important economic foundation for Chola power.

title: Which Chola ruler is generally regarded as the last major ruler of the dynasty?
description: Identify the later Chola ruler whose reign is associated with the final phase of Chola power.
hint: His reign ended in the early 13th century.
summary: Rajendra Chola III is generally regarded as the last Chola ruler.
